html:
The Donghu, "Eastern Hu", were a confederation of nomad tribes on the eastern steppe, in what is now eastern Inner Mongolia and western Manchuria. The map shows them in 400 BCE.

Chinese sources place them north of the state of Yan, which fought and traded with them. They herded horses, cattle and sheep. At their height they were stronger than their western neighbours, the Xiongnu.

That changed around 206 BCE. The new Xiongnu ruler Modu Chanyu at first gave the Donghu what they asked for, a fine horse and one of his wives. When they demanded land, he attacked and crushed them. The survivors split into two peoples, the Wuhuan and the Xianbei. The Xianbei later dominated the steppe and founded dynasties in north China, among them the Northern Wei.
sum: The Donghu, "Eastern Hu", were a confederation of nomad tribes on the eastern steppe, in what is now eastern Inner Mongolia and western Manchuria. The map shows them in 400 BCE.
